questions.question: What are the products in a reaction where an acid reacts with a base?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Salt and water**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A reaction in which an **acid** reacts with a **base** is termed a **Neutralization reaction**.
 
• In this process, the **hydrogen ions (H+)** from the acid and the **hydroxide ions (OH-)** from the base combine to form **water (H2O)**.
 
• The remaining part of the acid (anion) and the base (cation) combine to produce an **ionic compound** known as a **salt**.
 
• The general chemical equation for this reaction is: **Acid + Base → Salt + Water**. ***Hence, the correct option is Salt and water.***
 
• Neutralization reactions are typically **exothermic**, meaning **heat** is evolved during the reaction, which often raises the temperature of the reaction mixture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Examples of Neutralization:**

 
 
• The reaction between **Hydrochloric acid (HCl)** and **Sodium hydroxide (NaOH)** produces **Sodium chloride (NaCl)** and **water**. The formula is: **HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H2O**.
 
• Another common example is the reaction between **Sulfuric acid (H2SO4)** and **Potassium hydroxide (KOH)** to form **Potassium sulfate (K2SO4)** and **water**.
 
 
 
• **Nature of Salts:**
 
 
• If a **strong acid** reacts with a **strong base**, the resulting salt is **neutral** (pH value of **7**).
 
• A **strong acid** reacting with a **weak base** produces an **acidic salt** (pH value **less than 7**).
 
• A **weak acid** reacting with a **strong base** results in a **basic salt** (pH value **greater than 7**).
 
 
 
• **Real-world Applications:**
 
 
• **Indigestion:** Our stomach produces **hydrochloric acid** to digest food. Excess acid causes **acidity**, which is neutralized by taking **antacids** like **Milk of Magnesia** (Magnesium hydroxide), which is a **base**.
 
• **Ant Stings:** The sting of an ant contains **formic acid**. The effect of the sting can be neutralized by rubbing moist **baking soda** (sodium hydrogen carbonate) or **calamine solution** (zinc carbonate), which are **basic** in nature.
 
• **Soil Treatment:** Plants do not grow well if the **soil** is too acidic or too basic. Acidic soil is treated with **bases** like **quicklime** (calcium oxide) or **slaked lime** (calcium hydroxide).
 
• **Factory Waste:** Many **factories** discharge acidic wastes. These are neutralized by adding **basic substances** before being disposed of into water bodies to protect **aquatic life**.

questions.question: Who among the following kings acquired the title of ‘Dakshinapatheshvara’ (lord of the south)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pulakesin II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pulakesin II** was the most illustrious and powerful ruler of the **Chalukya dynasty** of **Vatapi** (modern-day **Badami** in **Karnataka**). He reigned from approximately **610 CE to 642 CE**.
 
• He is most famously known for acquiring the title **Dakshinapatheshvara** (Lord of the South) after his decisive victory over **Harshavardhana**, the ruler of **Kanauj**, on the banks of the **Narmada River** around **618-619 CE**.
 
• The primary source of information regarding his reign is the **Aihole inscription**, which was composed in **Sanskrit** by his court poet **Ravikirti**. This eulogy (Prashasti) details his military campaigns and the extent of his empire.
 
• By defeating **Harsha**, who was known as **Uttarapatheshvara** (Lord of the North), **Pulakesin II** established the **Narmada River** as the boundary between the northern and southern empires of India.
 
• Apart from **Dakshinapatheshvara**, he assumed other grand titles such as **Parameshwara** (Supreme Lord), **Satyashraya** (Abode of Truth), and **Prithvivallabha** (Lover of the Earth).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Upagupta**:

 
 
• **Upagupta** was a famous **Buddhist monk** who lived during the **3rd century BCE**.
 
• Historical traditions suggest that he was the spiritual teacher of the **Mauryan Emperor Ashoka** and influenced him to embrace **Buddhism** following the **Kalinga War**. Unlike the other options, he was a religious figure rather than a king.
 
 
 
• **Kharavela**:
 
 
• **Kharavela** was the third ruler of the **Mahameghavahana dynasty** of **Kalinga** (modern-day **Odisha**) during the **1st or 2nd century BCE**.
 
• He is known through the **Hathigumpha inscription** at **Udayagiri**. He was a follower of **Jainism** and assumed titles like **Kalinga-adhipati** (Lord of Kalinga) and **Chakravartin**.
 
 
 
• **Mahapadma Nanda**:
 
 
• **Mahapadma Nanda** was the founder of the **Nanda dynasty** in **Magadha** in the **4th century BCE**.
 
• He is described in the **Puranas** as **Sarvakshatrantaka** (uprooter of all Kshatriyas) and **Ekarat** (the sole monarch). He is often credited with creating the first great empire in North Indian history.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Conflict with the Pallavas**: While **Pulakesin II** dominated much of the **Deccan**, his reign ended in a tragic conflict with the **Pallava dynasty**. He was eventually defeated and killed by the Pallava king **Narasimhavarman I**, who subsequently took the title **Vatapikonda** (Conqueror of Vatapi).
 
• **Diplomatic Relations**: **Pulakesin II** is noted for his international diplomacy; he reportedly sent an embassy to the court of the **Persian King Khusrau II** in **625 CE**, highlighting the global reach of the **Chalukyan Empire**.
 
• **Xuanzang's Visit**: The famous **Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang** visited the kingdom of **Pulakesin II** in **641 CE** and left detailed accounts praising the king's power, the efficiency of his administration, and the bravery of his subjects.

questions.question: ‘Jhanjhar’ is a popular dance of which of the following Indian state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jharkhand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Jhanjhar dance** is a vibrant and rhythmic folk dance primarily performed in the state of **Jharkhand**, specifically within the tribal regions.
 
• It is traditionally associated with the **Munda** and **Santhal** tribes, who use this dance form to celebrate social gatherings and seasonal changes.
 
• The dance derives its name from the **Jhanjh**, which is a traditional musical instrument consisting of a pair of **brass cymbals** that produce a rhythmic metallic sound.
 
• The performance is characterized by the high-energy movements of the dancers who move in **circular or semi-circular formations**, mirroring the unity and collective spirit of the tribal community.
 
• It is often performed during significant cultural festivals such as **Sarhul** and **Karma**, which are dedicated to nature and the deities of the forest.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Folk Dances of Jharkhand:**

 
 
• **Chhau Dance:** Specifically the **Seraikella Chhau**, it is a famous masked dance that depicts stories from the **Mahabharata** and **Ramayana**. It was added to the **UNESCO** Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in **2010**.
 
• **Paika Dance:** A martial folk dance performed by the **Munda** community, where dancers carry **swords and shields** to display military bravery.
 
• **Karma Dance:** Performed during the **Karma festival** in the month of **Bhado** (August-September), it involves the worshipping of the **Karam tree** which symbolizes fertility and prosperity.
 
• **Santhali Dance:** Usually performed by the **Santhal** tribe during the **Sohrai** and **Baha** festivals, characterized by intricate footwork and the use of the **Madar** (drum).
 
 
 
• **Geographical and Cultural Context:**
 
 
• **Jharkhand** was officially formed on **15 November 2000**, after being carved out from the southern part of **Bihar**.
 
• The state is known as the **"Land of Forests"** and is situated on the **Chota Nagpur Plateau**, which influences its unique tribal art forms and lifestyle.
 
• The primary musical instruments used in Jharkhand folk music include the **Nagada**, **Dhol**, **Bansi** (flute), and **Turi**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Tribal Festivals:** The **Sarhul** festival is the most popular tribal festival in **Jharkhand**, celebrated when the **Sal trees** get new flowers, marking the beginning of the New Year for the tribes.
 
• **Socio-Economic Significance:** These folk dances like **Jhanjhar** are not merely entertainment but are essential for maintaining the oral traditions and cultural history of the **32 recognized tribes** of the state.
 
• **Global Recognition:** Tribal art from Jharkhand, including **Sohrai and Khovar painting**, received the **Geographical Indication (GI) tag** in **2020**, further highlighting the state's rich heritage alongside its performing arts.

questions.question: The ‘International Kite Festival’ in Gujarat coincides with which festival?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Makar Sankranti**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **International Kite Festival**, also known as **Uttarayan**, is one of the most vibrant festivals celebrated in the state of **Gujarat**. It marks the day when winter begins to turn into summer.
 
• This festival specifically coincides with **Makar Sankranti**, which is the day the **Sun** transitions into the zodiac sign of **Makara** (Capricorn).
 
• Since **1989**, the city of **Ahmedabad** has hosted the **International Kite Festival**, which attracts professional kite flyers and enthusiasts from various **countries** across the globe.
 
• The festival is typically observed on **January 14** every year. During this time, the skies over cities like **Ahmedabad**, **Surat**, **Vadodara**, and **Rajkot** are filled with thousands of colorful kites from dawn until late at night.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Makar Sankranti.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Makar Sankranti Significance:**

 
 
• It is a **harvest festival** celebrated in almost all parts of **India** under different names. In **Tamil Nadu**, it is celebrated as **Pongal**; in **Punjab**, as **Maghi**; and in **Assam**, as **Magh Bihu**.
 
• The festival marks the **solstice** and the beginning of the **Sun's** six-month-long journey towards the north (**Uttarayan**).
 
 
 
• **Description of Other Options:**
 
 
• **Holi**: Known as the **Festival of Colors**, it celebrates the arrival of spring and the victory of good over evil. It usually falls in the month of **March** (Phalguna). ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Diwali**: The **Festival of Lights**, signifying the return of **Lord Rama** to Ayodhya. It is celebrated in **October** or **November** (Kartika). ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Krishna Janmashtami**: This festival marks the birth of **Lord Krishna**, the eighth avatar of Vishnu. It is usually celebrated in **August** or **September**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Cultural Impact:**
 
 
• The **International Kite Festival** provides a massive boost to the local economy. The **kite-making industry** in **Gujarat** provides employment to thousands of artisans who create specialized kites and **Manja** (the thread coated with powdered glass).
 
• Special delicacies like **Undhiyu** (a spicy, baked mix of winter vegetables), **Jalebi**, and **Til Laddu** (sesame sweets) are traditionally prepared and consumed during this period.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Venue:** While the entire state celebrates, the **Sabarmati Riverfront** in **Ahmedabad** is the primary venue for the official international event organized by the **Gujarat Tourism Board**.
 
• **Tukkal:** At night, people fly kites with lanterns attached to them, known as **Tukkals**, which create a spectacular view of the night sky.
 
• **Global Participation:** In recent years, the festival has seen participation from over **50 countries**, including **USA**, **UK**, **Canada**, **Brazil**, **Australia**, and **Japan**, showcasing unique kite designs like dragon kites and sculptural kites.

questions.question: Who was one of Sirajuddaulah's commander that played a significant role in the Sirajuddaulah's defeat at the Battle of Plassey?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mir Jafar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mir Jafar** (Mir Muhammad Jafar Ali Khan) served as the **Commander-in-Chief** of the **Bengal army** under **Nawab Sirajuddaulah**.
 
• He played a treacherous role during the **Battle of Plassey**, which took place on **June 23, 1757**. He had entered into a secret pact with the **British East India Company**, represented by **Robert Clive**.
 
• During the battle, a large section of the Nawab's army under **Mir Jafar's** command did not take part in the fighting, ensuring the **Nawab's defeat**.
 
• In exchange for his betrayal, the **British** promised to make him the next **Nawab of Bengal**. After the victory, he was installed as a **puppet ruler** by the company.
 
• His name has since become synonymous with **treachery** in the Indian subcontinent due to his role in facilitating **British colonial rule** in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Alivardi Khan**:

 
 
• He was the **Nawab of Bengal** from **1740 to 1756**.
 
• He was the **grandfather** of **Sirajuddaulah** and successfully defended his territory against **Maratha invasions** multiple times.
 
 
 
• **Jagat Seth**:
 
 
• He was a title held by a very wealthy **banking family** in **Murshidabad**, Bengal.
 
• The **Jagat Seth** of the time, **Mehtab Chand**, was a key conspirator alongside **Mir Jafar** and the British to overthrow **Sirajuddaulah** due to the Nawab's strained relations with the merchant class.
 
 
 
• **Sirajuddaulah**:
 
 
• He was the last **independent Nawab of Bengal**.
 
• His reign was marked by conflict with the **British** over the misuse of **trade privileges** (Dastaks) and the fortification of **Fort William** in **Calcutta** without his permission.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Battle of Plassey**: This was a decisive victory of the **British East India Company** over the **Nawab of Bengal** and his **French allies**. It is considered the starting point of **British political supremacy** in India.
 
• **Robert Clive**: Often called **Clive of India**, he was the primary architect of the British victory at Plassey through **military strategy** and **political intrigue**.
 
• **Mir Madan and Mohan Lal**: Unlike **Mir Jafar**, these were the **loyal commanders** of **Sirajuddaulah** who fought bravely and died on the battlefield defending the Nawab.
 
• **Consequences**: After the battle, the **British** gained the **Diwani rights** (right to collect revenue) in Bengal, Bihar, and Odisha following the subsequent **Battle of Buxar** in **1764**, solidifying their control over the richest province of India.

questions.question: Which of the following gas is used as fuels in vehicles these days?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Compressed natural gas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Compressed Natural Gas (CNG)** is the primary gas used as a fuel in vehicles these days due to its **eco-friendly** nature. It is primarily composed of **methane (CH4)**. ***Hence, option 1 is correct.***
 
• It is produced by compressing **natural gas** to less than **1%** of its standard atmospheric volume. This compression is usually done at a pressure of **20 to 25 MegaPascals (MPa)**.
 
• CNG is considered a "clean fuel" because it emits significantly lower levels of harmful pollutants such as **carbon monoxide (CO)**, **nitrogen oxides (NOx)**, and **particulate matter** compared to **petrol** or **diesel**.
 
• In **India**, the transition to CNG was significantly accelerated following a **Supreme Court** mandate in **1998**, which required all public transport in **Delhi** to switch to CNG to combat rising **air pollution** levels.
 
• The **ignition temperature** of CNG is approximately **540°C**, which is much higher than that of liquid fuels, making it a safer option as it is less likely to ignite accidentally in the event of a leak.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nitrogen gas**:

 
 
• While not used as a fuel, **Nitrogen** is increasingly used to **inflate vehicle tires**. Unlike regular air, nitrogen does not leak through tire walls as easily and helps maintain **tire pressure** for longer periods. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***
 
• It also keeps tires cooler during long drives, which improves **fuel efficiency** and extends the life of the rubber.
 
 
 
• **Liquefied petroleum gas (LPG)**:
 
 
• LPG is a mixture of **propane** and **butane**. While it is used as "Auto LPG" in some light vehicles, it is more commonly used as a **domestic fuel** for **cooking (LPG cylinders)** and heating. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect in the context of the most prominent modern vehicle fuel.***
 
• It is stored under moderate pressure in liquid form and has a high **calorific value**.
 
 
 
• **Helium gas**:
 
 
• **Helium** is an **inert, noble gas** that does not burn and cannot be used as a fuel. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***
 
• Its applications include **weather balloons**, **MRI scanners** (as a coolant), and **cryogenics** due to its extremely low boiling point.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Environmental Impact**: CNG reduces **carbon dioxide (CO2)** emissions by about **20-30%** compared to traditional fossil fuels, aiding in the reduction of the **carbon footprint**.
 
• **Fuel Economics**: CNG is generally much **cheaper** than petrol and diesel, providing better **mileage** and reducing the overall running cost of the vehicle.
 
• **Bharat Stage (BS) Norms**: In **India**, the government has implemented **Bharat Stage VI (BS-VI)** emission standards since **April 2020**, which further encourages the use of cleaner fuels like CNG and **Electric Vehicles (EVs)** to meet stringent environmental targets.
 
• **Safety Features**: Because CNG is **lighter than air**, it dissipates quickly upward in the event of a leak, unlike LPG which is heavier and tends to settle near the ground, creating a fire hazard.

questions.question: The International Space Station is a large space station in low earth orbit at about ____ Km from the Earth surface.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**400**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **International Space Station (ISS)** is a modular space station located in **Low Earth Orbit (LEO)**. It orbits at an average altitude of approximately **400 kilometers** (roughly **250 miles**) above the **Earth's surface**.
 
• It travels at a velocity of approximately **28,000 kilometers per hour** (**17,500 miles per hour**). At this incredible speed, the **ISS** completes one full orbit of the **Earth** every **90 to 93 minutes**, meaning the astronauts on board witness about **16 sunrises and sunsets** every **24 hours**.
 
• The construction of the station began in **1998** with the launch of the **Russian** module **Zarya**. Since then, various modules have been added by different participating nations to expand its living and laboratory space.
 
• The altitude of the **ISS** is not fixed; it fluctuates between **330 km** and **435 km** due to **atmospheric drag**. To maintain its orbit and prevent it from crashing into the atmosphere, the station requires periodic "re-boosts" using its own engines or those of docked spacecraft.
 
• The **ISS** serves as a unique **microgravity** and space environment research laboratory where scientific contributions are made in **astrobiology**, **astronomy**, **meteorology**, and **physics**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **International Collaboration:** The **ISS** is a joint project involving five participating space agencies: **NASA** (United States), **Roscosmos** (Russia), **JAXA** (Japan), **ESA** (Europe), and **CSA** (Canada). The ownership and use of the station are established by intergovernmental treaties and agreements.
 
• **Physical Characteristics:** The station is roughly the size of a **football field**, measuring about **109 meters** in length. It features large **solar arrays** that collect energy from the **Sun** to power its various systems and scientific experiments.
 
• **Human Occupation:** The **ISS** has been continuously inhabited since **November 2, 2000**. This represents the longest continuous human presence in **space**, surpassing the previous record held by the **Russian** space station **Mir**.
 
• **Scientific Utility:** One of the primary goals of the **ISS** is to provide a platform for long-term research that cannot be performed on **Earth**. This includes studying the effects of long-term **spaceflight** on the **human body**, which is critical for future missions to the **Moon** and **Mars**.
 
• **Observation from Earth:** Due to its size and the reflectivity of its **solar panels**, the **ISS** is the **third brightest object** in the night sky after the **Moon** and **Venus**. It can be seen with the naked eye from the ground as a steady, moving point of light.
 
• **Comparison with Other Orbits:**
 
 
• **Low Earth Orbit (LEO):** Extends up to **2,000 km**. This is where most satellites and the **ISS** reside.
 
• **Medium Earth Orbit (MEO):** Ranges from **2,000 km** to **35,786 km**. **GPS** satellites typically operate here at about **20,200 km**.
 
• **Geostationary Orbit (GEO):** Located at exactly **35,786 km**. Satellites here appear stationary over a fixed point on **Earth**, used mostly for **telecommunications** and **weather monitoring**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Microgravity:** Often mistakenly called "zero gravity," the **ISS** is actually in a state of **freefall**. The **gravity** at that altitude is still about **90%** of that on **Earth's surface**, but the station's forward motion keeps it falling "around" the planet rather than into it.
 
• **Water Recycling:** Because resources are limited, the **ISS** uses advanced life support systems that recycle about **93%** of all water on board, including **urine** and **sweat**, converting it back into drinkable water.
 
• **Zvezda Module:** This is the functional center of the **Russian** segment, providing life support systems and the engines used for **orbital altitude** adjustments.

questions.question: The total number of women contesting general elections in the country has increased to ____ in 2024.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• During the **18th Lok Sabha Elections** held in **2024**, the proportion of women candidates contesting the polls reached approximately **10%** of the total candidates.
 
• Out of a total of **8,360 candidates** who participated in the general elections across the country, **797** were women.
 
• This marks a progressive increase from the **2019 General Elections**, where the total number of women candidates was **726**, accounting for about **9%** of the total contestants.
 
• The **Election Commission of India** data indicates that while the absolute number of women participants has risen, they still represent a relatively small fraction of the total political field.
 
• Major political parties showed varying levels of representation; the **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)** fielded **69** women, while the **Indian National Congress (INC)** fielded **41** women candidates.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Historical Representation Trends**:

 
 
• In the **1st Lok Sabha** elections in **1952**, women candidates were only about **4.4%** of the total pool.
 
• The **2024** mark of **10%** is one of the highest recorded in **Indian parliamentary history**, though it falls short of the proposed legislative targets.
 
 
 
• **Legislative Framework**:
 
 
• The **Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam** (the **128th Constitutional Amendment Bill**) was passed in **September 2023**.
 
• This landmark legislation mandates **33% reservation** for women in the **Lok Sabha** and **State Legislative Assemblies**, but its implementation is tied to the next **delimitation exercise**.
 
 
 
• **Electoral Outcomes**:
 
 
• Despite the increase in contestants to **10%**, the number of women actually elected to the **Lok Sabha** in **2024** stood at **74**.
 
• This is a slight decrease from the **2019 elections**, where **78** women were elected to the lower house of **Parliament**.

questions.question: Why does a paper cup not burn when filled with water and heated?

options.text: The water evaporates and cools the paper
The water absorbs the heat, preventing the paper from reaching its ignition temperature
The paper becomes fireproof when wet
The water creates steam, which extinguishes the flame

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The water absorbs the heat, preventing the paper from reaching its ignition temperature**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phenomenon is primarily governed by the principles of **heat transfer** and the specific **ignition temperature** of materials.
 
• **Ignition temperature** is defined as the minimum temperature at which a combustible substance catches fire; for ordinary paper, this is approximately **233 degrees Celsius** (451 degrees Fahrenheit).
 
• When a paper cup is filled with water, the heat energy supplied by the flame is rapidly conducted through the thin paper to the **water** inside.
 
• Water has an exceptionally high **specific heat capacity**, meaning it can absorb a large amount of thermal energy before its own temperature rises significantly.
 
• As long as there is water present, the heat is used to raise the water temperature or maintain it at the **boiling point of 100 degrees Celsius**.
 
• Because **100 degrees Celsius** is much lower than the paper's ignition threshold, the paper never becomes hot enough to burn.
 
• The process of **conduction** ensures that the paper and water remain in **thermal equilibrium**, effectively cooling the paper surface.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phase Change and Latent Heat**:

 
 
• Once the water reaches its boiling point, any additional heat supplied is consumed as **latent heat of vaporization** to convert liquid water into steam.
 
• This phase transition happens at a constant temperature of **100 degrees Celsius**, providing a thermal ceiling that protects the paper from charring.
 
 
 
• **The Fire Triangle**:
 
 
• Combustion requires three components: **Fuel**, **Oxygen**, and **Heat** (sufficient to reach the ignition point). By removing the accumulation of heat, the **fire triangle** is broken.
 
 
 
• **Thermal Conductivity**:
 
 
• While paper itself is not a great conductor, its **thickness** is minimal in a cup, allowing heat to pass through it almost instantly into the liquid medium.

questions.question: Which of the following economic activity is included in the primary sector?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fishing**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **primary sector** of the economy is based on the direct extraction and use of **natural resources** from the environment.
 
• It forms the base for all other products that we subsequently make, acting as the provider of **raw materials** for the industrial sector.
 
• **Fishing** is a quintessential primary activity because it involves the harvesting of **biological resources** directly from water bodies like oceans, rivers, and lakes.
 
• Other major activities included in this sector are **agriculture**, **forestry**, **mining**, and **animal husbandry**.
 
• In developing nations like **India**, the primary sector remains a significant contributor to **employment**, even as its share in the **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** may fluctuate compared to the service sector.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Manufacturing**:

 
 
• Belongs to the **secondary sector**, which involves the transformation of raw materials into finished goods.
 
• It utilizes **industrial processes** and machinery to add value to primary products, such as turning cotton into fabric.
 
 
 
• **Healthcare**:
 
 
• Classified under the **tertiary sector**, also known as the **service sector**.
 
• It provides essential **intangible services** to individuals rather than producing physical commodities.
 
 
 
• **Trade and Logistics**:
 
 
• These are also **tertiary sector** activities that facilitate the distribution and exchange of goods.
 
• **Logistics** focuses on the **transportation** and storage of products, ensuring they reach the consumer efficiently from the point of production.

questions.question: Which of the following activity is responsible for disturbance of the balance between the process of soil formation and soil erosion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Deforestation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Deforestation** involves the large-scale removal of forest cover, which serves as a natural protective shield for the **earth's surface**.
 
• The **root systems** of trees play a critical role in **soil conservation** by binding soil particles together, thereby preventing them from being washed away by **surface runoff** or blown away by **wind**.
 
• When vegetation is removed, the **topsoil** is exposed to the direct impact of heavy rainfall, which leads to **sheet erosion** and **gully erosion**, significantly accelerating the rate of soil loss.
 
• While **soil formation** is a slow geological process taking hundreds of years to produce a thin layer of fertile soil, **deforestation** can lead to the removal of this layer in a very short span, thus disturbing the **natural equilibrium**.
 
• Human activities like **overgrazing**, **construction**, and **mining** often accompany deforestation, further aggravating the **imbalance** between soil accumulation and degradation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Afforestation**:

 
 
• Refers to the process of **planting trees** on land that has not been recently forested.
 
• It acts as a **remedial measure** to restore the balance by increasing **canopy cover** and anchoring the soil.
 
 
 
• **Organic Farming**:
 
 
• A method of crop production that avoids **synthetic fertilizers** and pesticides.
 
• It improves **soil texture** and **moisture retention**, which naturally reduces the risk of erosion.
 
 
 
• **Intercropping**:
 
 
• The practice of growing **two or more crops** in proximity in the same field.
 
• This ensures the ground is covered throughout the year, protecting it from **weathering agents**.

questions.question: The National Capital Goods Policy in India was launched in ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2016**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Capital Goods Policy** was officially launched by the **Ministry of Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises** in **February 2016**.
 
• It serves as the first-ever integrated policy for the **Capital Goods sector** in India, aimed at making the country a global hub for the design, manufacture, and assembly of capital goods.
 
• The policy envisions increasing the total production of capital goods from approximately **Rs 2,30,000 crore** in **2014-15** to **Rs 7,50,000 crore** by the year **2025**.
 
• A critical objective of the policy is to improve the **export share** of the sector from the current **27%** to at least **40%** of the total production.
 
• It aims to generate significant **employment opportunities**, targeting an increase in the workforce from **8.4 million** to **30 million** by **2025**.
 
• The policy focuses on various sub-sectors including **machine tools**, **textile machinery**, **earthmoving and mining equipment**, and **power equipment**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Strategic Importance of Capital Goods**:

 
 
• Capital goods are the machinery and equipment used to produce other goods; therefore, they are often referred to as the **mother of all manufacturing sectors**.
 
• The sector contributes roughly **12%** to the total **manufacturing output** in India.
 
 
 
• **Policy Implementation & Initiatives**:
 
 
• **Technology Acquisition Fund Scheme (TAFS)**: Designed to help **MSMEs** acquire advanced technologies from abroad or through domestic **R&D**.
 
• **Skill Development**: Creation of specialized **Sector Skill Councils** to provide high-end technical training.
 
• **Standardization**: Mandatory adoption of **International Standards** to ensure Indian products are competitive in the global market.
 
 
 
• **Vision Alignment**:
 
 
• The policy is a crucial component of the **Make in India** initiative, aiming to increase the manufacturing sector's contribution to the **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** to **25%**.

• The **Ankle hold** is a defensive tactic primarily executed by **corner defenders** (Right Corner or Left Corner). It involves the defender catching the raider's ankle with a firm grip to prevent them from reaching the **midline**.
 
• The **Knee hold** is another specialized defensive maneuver where the defender targets the raider's knee to lock their movement, making it difficult for the raider to escape or use their **leg strength** to pull towards safety.
 
• These techniques are essential components of the scoring system in professional leagues like the **Pro Kabaddi League** (PKL), where successful tackles earn the defending team **one point**.
 
• Defenders use these maneuvers collectively to execute a **Chain Tackle** or a **Block**, which are critical strategies used to neutralize the offensive **raider**.

• **FX-CLEAR** is an electronic, anonymous order-matching system for the **Inter-bank Foreign Exchange** market in India.
 
• The platform was officially launched on **August 7, 2003**, to facilitate efficient and transparent trading in the **USD/INR** currency pair.
 
• It was developed and is managed by **Clearcorp Dealing Systems (India) Limited**, which is a wholly-owned subsidiary of the **Clearing Corporation of India Limited (CCIL)**.
 
• The system provides a **blind order-matching** environment where the identities of the buying and selling banks are kept confidential until the trade is executed, thereby minimizing **market impact costs**.
 
• The launch of **FX-CLEAR** marked a significant shift from traditional **voice-based brokering** to a technologically advanced electronic trading infrastructure for the Indian banking sector.

• It provides **guaranteed settlement** for trades executed on the **FX-CLEAR** platform, acting as a **Central Counterparty (CCP)** to mitigate settlement risk.
 
 
 
• **Clearcorp Dealing Systems (India) Limited:**

questions.question: Where is the 'Thousand Pillar' Temple located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Telangana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Thousand Pillar Temple**, also known as the **Rudreshwara Swamy Temple**, is a historic Hindu temple located in the town of **Hanamkonda**, which is part of the **Warangal** district in the state of **Telangana**, India.
 
• It was constructed in **1163 AD** by the great **King Rudra Deva** of the **Kakatiya Dynasty**, representing the peak of **Kakatiyan architectural** brilliance.
 
• The temple is dedicated to three primary deities: **Lord Shiva** (Rudreshwara), **Lord Vishnu**, and **Lord Surya**. Because it houses three shrines, it is technically known as a **Trikutalyam**.
 
• The structure is famous for its **star-shaped** architecture and contains **one thousand pillars**, which are intricately carved. Remarkably, the pillars are arranged such that they do not obstruct the view of the central deity from any point within the temple.
 
• The temple was built in the **Chalukyan style** of architecture and is adorned with perforated stone screens and exquisite sculptures of **elephants** and other mythical creatures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kakatiya Dynasty:**

 
 
• The **Kakatiyas** were a prominent South Indian dynasty that ruled most of the **eastern Deccan** region comprising modern-day **Telangana** and **Andhra Pradesh** between the **12th and 14th centuries**.
 
• Their capital was **Orugallu**, now known as **Warangal**. They were great patrons of art and architecture, responsible for other monuments like the **Warangal Fort** and the **Ramappa Temple**.
 
 
 
• **Architecture and Material:**
 
 
• The temple is built on a **1-meter high platform**. It features a massive **monolithic Nandi** (bull) carved out of a single piece of **black basalt** stone.
 
• This **Nandi** is unique because it faces the **Lord Shiva** shrine, which is a common feature in Shaivite temples, but the craftsmanship here is considered among the finest in **India**.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance:**
 
 
• The temple faced significant destruction during the invasion of the **Deccan** by the **Delhi Sultanate** (led by the **Tughlaq dynasty**) in the **14th century**.
 
• The **Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)** has undertaken extensive restoration projects, particularly for the **Kalyana Mandapam** (marriage hall), to preserve its structural integrity.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ramappa Temple Connection:**

 
 
• While the **Thousand Pillar Temple** is a major landmark, its contemporary, the **Ramappa Temple** in **Palampet**, was inscribed as a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** in **2021**. Both share the distinct **Kakatiya** style of using **sandbox foundations** and **floating bricks**.
 
 
 
• **Tourism and Culture:**
 
 
• The temple remains an active place of worship and a major tourist attraction in the **Deccan Plateau**. It is located approximately **150 km** from **Hyderabad**.
 
• The **Kala Thoranam** (ornamental gateway) found in the nearby **Warangal Fort** is so iconic that it has been adopted as the official **State Emblem of Telangana**.

questions.question: Where is the tomb of Sher Shah Suri located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sasaram**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The tomb of **Sher Shah Suri** is a magnificent example of **Indo-Islamic architecture** located in **Sasaram**, in the **Rohtas district** of **Bihar**.
 
• It was constructed in memory of Emperor **Sher Shah Suri**, a Pathan from Bihar who founded the **Suri Empire** in northern India after defeating the Mughal Empire.
 
• The structure was designed by the renowned architect **Mir Muhammad Aliwal Khan** and was completed between **1540 and 1545 AD**.
 
• It is famously known as a "water tomb" because it is situated in the middle of a large, artificial square **lake**, standing on a stone plinth with domes and kiosks.
 
• The tomb is built of **red sandstone** and features an **octagonal** plan, which was a signature style of the **Lodi** and **Suri** dynasties, and it is often described as the second **Taj Mahal** of India due to its grandeur.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sher Shah Suri (Reign: 1540–1545):**

 
 
• Born as **Farid Khan**, he assumed the title **Sher Shah** after killing a tiger single-handedly.
 
• He defeated the Mughal Emperor **Humayun** in the **Battle of Chausa** (**1539**) and the **Battle of Kannauj** (**1540**), forcing him into exile.
 
• He is credited with the introduction of the **Rupiya**, which is the precursor to the modern Indian Rupee.
 
• He reconstructed and extended the **Grand Trunk Road** (then known as **Sadak-e-Azam**), connecting **Chittagong** (Bangladesh) to **Kabul** (Afghanistan).
 
 
 
• **Other Options Analysis:**
 
 
• **Sikandra**: Located in **Agra**, **Uttar Pradesh**, it is the site of the **Tomb of Akbar**, the third Mughal Emperor. It features a unique blend of Hindu, Christian, Islamic, Buddhist, and Jain architectural motifs.
 
• **Lahore**: This city in **Pakistan** houses the **Tomb of Jahangir**, located in **Shahdara Bagh**. It also contains the tombs of **Nur Jahan** and **Asif Khan**.
 
• **Aurangabad**: Located in **Maharashtra**, it is home to the **Bibi Ka Maqbara**, which is the tomb of **Dilras Banu Begum**, the wife of Mughal Emperor **Aurangzeb**. It was commissioned in **1660**.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• Sher Shah Suri died in a gunpowder explosion during the siege of **Kalinjar Fort** in **1545**.
 
• His tomb represents a transitional phase in Indian architecture, moving from the simpler **Sultanate** styles to the more decorative **Mughal** era structures.
 
• The tomb was designated as a site of national importance under the **Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act**.

questions.question: In a compound like water, the mass ratio of hydrogen to oxygen is always ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1:8**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a chemical compound like **water (H2O)**, the elements hydrogen and oxygen are always combined in a fixed proportion by mass, regardless of the source of the water.
 
• A single molecule of water consists of **two atoms of hydrogen** and **one atom of oxygen**.
 
• To find the mass ratio, we use the **atomic masses** of the constituent elements: the **atomic mass of Hydrogen (H)** is approximately **1 unit (u)**, and the **atomic mass of Oxygen (O)** is approximately **16 units (u)**.
 
• The total mass of hydrogen in the molecule is **2 x 1 = 2 units**, and the total mass of oxygen is **16 units**.
 
• The ratio of the mass of hydrogen to the mass of oxygen is **2:16**. When simplified by dividing both sides by **2**, the ratio becomes **1:8**. ***Hence, the ratio of hydrogen to oxygen by mass is always 1:8.***
 
• This implies that if **9 grams** of water is decomposed, **1 gram** of hydrogen gas and **8 grams** of oxygen gas will always be obtained.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Law of Constant Proportions**: This principle is also known as the **Law of Definite Proportions**. It was formulated by the French chemist **Joseph Proust** in **1799**. The law states that a given chemical compound always contains its component elements in a fixed ratio by mass and does not depend on its source or method of preparation.
 
• **Ammonia (NH3)**: Another classic example is ammonia. In **NH3**, nitrogen and hydrogen are always present in the ratio **14:3** by mass. This is because the **atomic mass of Nitrogen** is **14** and there are three hydrogen atoms with a total mass of **3**.
 
• **Carbon Dioxide (CO2)**: In carbon dioxide, the ratio of carbon to oxygen by mass is **12:32** (since **C=12** and **O=16x2=32**), which simplifies to **3:8**.
 
• **Dalton's Atomic Theory**: This law provided significant evidence for **John Dalton's** atomic theory, specifically the postulate that compounds are formed by the combination of atoms of different elements in simple whole-number ratios.
 
• **Fundamental Laws of Chemical Combination**: The Law of Constant Proportions is one of the three basic laws of stoichiometry, alongside the **Law of Conservation of Mass** (proposed by **Antoine Lavoisier**) and the **Law of Multiple Proportions**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• It is important to distinguish between the **ratio by number of atoms** and the **ratio by mass**. In water, the ratio by number of atoms is **2:1** (Hydrogen to Oxygen), while the ratio by mass is **1:8**.
 
• The discovery of **isotopes** later showed that the law is not strictly universal in all cases, as different isotopes of the same element have different masses. However, for most practical chemical calculations and naturally occurring mixtures of isotopes, the law remains highly accurate.
 
• In **modern chemistry**, these mass ratios are essential for determining the **empirical formulas** and **molecular formulas** of unknown substances during chemical analysis.

questions.question: Dmitri Mendeleev was unable to assign the correct position to which element?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hydrogen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dmitri Mendeleev** was unable to assign a fixed or correct position to **Hydrogen** in his **Periodic Table** because of its unique electronic configuration and dual chemical nature.
 
• **Hydrogen** resembles **Alkali Metals** (Group 1) because, like **Lithium**, **Sodium**, and **Potassium**, it combines with **Halogens**, **Oxygen**, and **Sulphur** to form compounds having similar formulas.
 
• On the other hand, **Hydrogen** also resembles **Halogens** (Group 17) because it exists as a **diatomic molecule** (H2) and forms **covalent compounds** with metals and non-metals.
 
• Just like **Halogens**, it requires only one electron to attain the stable configuration of the nearest **noble gas** (Helium).
 
• Due to these similarities with two different groups, **Mendeleev** could not justify a single specific position for **Hydrogen** based on his periodic law of **atomic masses**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mendeleev's Periodic Law:** Formulated in **1869**, it stated that the physical and chemical properties of elements are a **periodic function** of their **atomic masses**. At that time, only **63 elements** were known.
 
• **Limitations of Mendeleev’s Table:**
 
 
• **Position of Isotopes:** Since **isotopes** of an element have different **atomic masses**, they should have been placed in different slots, but they weren't.
 
• **Anomalous Pairs:** In some cases, an element with a higher **atomic mass** was placed before an element with a lower atomic mass (e.g., **Cobalt** before **Nickel**) to maintain chemical similarity.
 
 
 
• **Modern Periodic Table:** This issue was largely resolved in **1913** when **Henry Moseley** showed that **atomic number** (the number of protons) is a more fundamental property than **atomic mass**.
 
• In the **Modern Periodic Table**, **Hydrogen** is usually placed at the top of **Group 1**, but it is often treated as a unique element because it does not fit perfectly with any single group.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Hydrogen (H):** It is the **first element** in the periodic table with an **atomic number of 1**. It is the lightest and most abundant chemical substance in the universe, constituting roughly **75%** of all normal matter.
 
• **Helium (He):** Unlike **Hydrogen**, **Helium** is a **noble gas** with a completely filled valence shell. It was discovered in **1868** and was later assigned to **Group 18** (or Group 0) of the periodic table due to its inertness.
 
• **Chlorine (Cl):** It is a member of the **Halogen** family (Group 17) with **atomic number 17**. It is a highly reactive gas and was well-placed in **Mendeleev's** table based on its valency of 1.
 
• **Oxygen (O):** With **atomic number 8**, it belongs to the **Chalcogen** group. **Mendeleev** used the formulas of **oxides** as a primary criterion for classifying elements in his table.

questions.question: M.S. Subbulakshmi is the first ____ with the Bharat Ratna in 1998.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**musicians**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **M.S. Subbulakshmi** (**Madurai Shanmukhavadivu Subbulakshmi**) was a legendary **Carnatic singer** from **India**.
 
• In **1998**, she became the **first musician** to be ever honored with the **Bharat Ratna**, which is **India's highest civilian award**. ***Hence, the correct answer is musicians.***
 
• She was a pioneer in the field of music and was also the **first Indian musician** to receive the **Ramon Magsaysay Award** in **1974**, often considered Asia's Nobel Prize.
 
• She made history by being the **first Indian musician** to perform at the **United Nations General Assembly** in **1966**.
 
• Her contribution to the **classical music** of **South India** and her spiritual renderings of **hymns and bhajans** earned her the title of "**Queen of Music**," a name given to her by **Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Early Life and Background**:

 
 
• She was born on **September 16, 1916**, in **Madurai**, **Tamil Nadu**.
 
• She grew up in a family of musicians and started her training in **Carnatic music** at a very young age under the guidance of her mother, **Shanmukhavadivu**.
 
 
 
• **Musical Career and Contributions**:
 
 
• She was known for her exceptional mastery over **Sanskrit**, **Tamil**, **Telugu**, **Kannada**, and **Hindi** compositions.
 
• Her most famous recitals include the **Venkateswara Suprabhatam**, **Vishnu Sahasranamam**, and **Bhajagovindam**, which are still widely played across **Indian** households.
 
• She also acted in a few films, most notably **Meera** (**1945**), which brought her national fame across both **North** and **South India**.
 
 
 
• **Other Notable Awards**:
 
 
• She received the **Padma Bhushan** in **1954**.
 
• She was awarded the **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award** in **1956**.
 
• In **1975**, she was honored with the **Padma Vibhushan**, the **second-highest civilian award in India**.
 
 
 
• **Contrast with Other Options**:
 
 
• **Sportsperson**: **Sachin Tendulkar** was the **first sportsperson** to receive the **Bharat Ratna** in **2014**.
 
• **Painter**: As of now, no **painter** has been awarded the **Bharat Ratna** for their work primarily in fine arts/painting.
 
• **Author**: While many recipients like **Rabindranath Tagore** (Nobel laureate) were writers, **Subbulakshmi** is specifically recognized as the first recipient from the **musical** fraternity.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Musicians with Bharat Ratna**:

 
 
• Following **M.S. Subbulakshmi**, other notable **musicians** who received the award include **Pandit Ravi Shankar** (**1999**), **Lata Mangeshkar** (**2001**), **Ustad Bismillah Khan** (**2001**), **Pandit Bhimsen Joshi** (**2009**), and **Bhupen Hazarika** (**2019**, posthumously).
 
 
 
• **Bharat Ratna Facts**:
 
 
• The **Bharat Ratna** was instituted in **1954**.
 
• It is awarded for exceptional service/performance of the highest order in any field of human endeavor.
 
• The recommendations for **Bharat Ratna** are made by the **Prime Minister** to the **President of India**.
